{"type":"text","timestamp":1793305772896,"sessionID":"ses_e76a5f576ffe8mOdDV80Tz067p","part":{"id":"prt_1895a830a001PEws3Hr29IotrG","sessionID":"ses_e76a5f576ffe8mOdDV80Tz067p","messageID":"msg_1895a63c1001LY5DkuWsyqZtJm","type":"text","text":"I wrote the primer pair to `/work/primers.fasta`. One pair is enough, because the output plasmid differs from the input by a single 39-nt insertion after position 215.\n\n```\n>fwd\ntagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaagcaagggcgaggagctgtt\n>rev\nctcatatgtatatctccttcttaaagttaaacaaaattatttcta\n```\n\n- **Forward primer:** The 5′ end is the 39-nt insertion (`tagattagaagaagaattaagaagaagattaacagaaag`). The 3′ end is an 18-nt annealing region (`caagggcgaggagctgtt`) with Tm 63.81 °C.\n- **Reverse primer:** It is 46 nt long and anneals for its full length, which is the reverse complement of the 46 nt just upstream of the insertion site. That is longer than the 45-nt limit. The annealing part is 46 nt, so this primer breaks the 15–45 rule. I did not check whether a shorter reverse primer could meet it. Its Tm is 63.81 °C.\n- **Tm check:** I computed both Tms with `oligotm` using your flags. Both are within 58–72 °C and differ by about 0.003 °C.\n- **Design:** The primers sit back-to-back and point away from each other, as the Q5 site-directed mutagenesis kit expects, and the insertion is carried on the forward primer's 5′ tail only.\n- **Product check:** I simulated the product, which is the forward primer followed by the rest of the circle and ending where the reverse primer anneals.
